recommendation_issues:
1. Instant growth: anchoring at the soles contradicts the blast model. The recommendation anchors growth at the soles but sizes the blast with a ball expanding about its centre. With sole anchoring, upward-moving surfaces sweep exactly 1/3 of the added volume at up to the head speed (Mach 3-4.5). Because Δp grows as u², energy into the air is about 2× (ball anchored at its base) to 4.3× (Rex-shaped column) the ball value. The local top pressure is about 2.4-2.9 MPa, not 2-3 atm. Either widen E_x, TNT and reach (reach ×1.3-1.6), or state that the ball model assumes growth about the centre.

2. Instant growth: momentum is missing (canon: momentum is never absorbed). With the soles fixed, the centre of mass rises at about half the head speed: about 700 m/s for Chicxulub pure size, a momentum of 3.3e9 kg·m/s. The ground must push 3.9e11 N, 4.7 GPa on Rex's grown 83 m² soles (twice that for Ollie's boots), which exceeds any rock strength in the data. Nothing can then pull him back, so he would be launched about 25 km up unless 'bolted to the planet' is on. The alternative, anchoring at the centre of mass, drives his feet about ΔH/2 into the ground at about 700 m/s. Gradual growth needs a matching lift-off check: T ≥ about √(πΔH/g), about 3 s for Chicxulub pure size. It is never binding next to the shove limit, but it should be computed. 'Ground ≈ 0' is right for the loop ratio only, not for the hazard.

3. Windows: use the existing 3.4-6.9 kPa band, not 6.9 kPa alone (100-220 m for Chicxulub pure size).

4. The 20 Pa preset uses the wrong measurement basis and the wrong label. USBM's 120 dB is on the 6 Hz high-pass meter; on the 0.1 Hz basis it is about 125 dB, about 36 Pa. A seconds-long growth pulse barely registers on a 6 Hz meter, and the source says rattling still occurs below the safe level, so 'nothing rattles' is false. It is also a stricter preset, not a 'higher' one. The window (3.4 kPa) and eardrum (34.5 kPa) presets are fast-rising blast thresholds and are not validated for a smooth pulse lasting seconds; label them that way.

5. Taylor k table: below about 0.3 c0 the surface factor rises toward the incompressible 1.5 ρ0u², not toward 1.16. The sphere value applies only when R_final ≫ R0 (growth time much longer than R0/c0 = 2.6 ms). Otherwise the planar ρ0c0u onset is the right estimate, as the researcher already uses for Krakatoa. Since t_x = 0.77 R_f/c0 always, say plainly that for modest k the planar value applies.

6. Bystander shove factor: 0.29 (equivalent-ball radius over height) is not Rex's geometry. Under sole anchoring, any point's outward speed is (its horizontal distance from the anchor ÷ H) × head speed; the tail tip, snout or arms may reach 0.5-0.8×.

7. Runaway multiplier: whether 1/(1 − f) applies at all depends on canon not yet given: is the work done on the air paid from the absorbed energy, or from the endless store? CLAUDE.md says to ask the owners rather than invent canon. Present it as an open question, not a computed multiplier.

8. The low end of Morgan 2022's 'range' (1e23 J) is the abstract's order-of-magnitude rounding of the same 5e23 J estimate, not a separate lower bound.

9. Krakatoa: 'any estimate adds under 51 kg' is wrong. The figures the researcher quotes go to 1.5 Gt (70 kg), and the source's extreme is about 12 Gt (about 560 kg).

10. The horizon crossing uses the engine's equivalent-ball radius. Label it a convention: a 3 m-tall body would plausibly need more mass to sit inside its own horizon.

11. Wording: 'OSHA allows' should be 'OSHA's Technical Manual describes'. 'The brief's strong-shock form' does not exist in the brief.

The core physics is otherwise sound: E/c² growth forms, the k_V/k_H sampling, the monopole with ground doubling, Baker's 2E rule and the pentolite upper limit beyond R̄ ≈ 2, the Newtonian and GR loop ratios, and the Bondi gate. All formulas are used within their stated validity apart from the points above.

Buildings, vehicles or trees inside the final footprint (equivalent radius 10 m for Chicxulub pure size, 99 m for the Sun-second; actual footprint shape unknown) are pushed over or crushed at any speed. Pinned people are already noted.

- Ollie-specific inputs: 3.06 m tall and 0.15 m² boot soles, so ground stresses are twice Rex's.

verdict:
Sources and arithmetic are sound. I re-fetched every cited source (NIST c and G, Harkrider & Press record and full PDF, Lobanovsky, Morgan 2022, IAU 2015, Rienstra & Hirschberg, USBM RI 8485, OSHA, Bohannon, both PMC reviews, NASA normal shock, Collins, Baker 1977, Lattimer & Prakash, the Courant & Friedrichs scan and OCR text, Trachenko, and Crossref for the three DOIs). All derived numbers reproduce to the stated precision, and my own Taylor solver matches theirs within 1%.

Corrections needed before building:
- Krakatoa energy spread: wrong high end (at least 6.3e18 J, extreme about 5e19 J, so up to 70 kg and possibly about 560 kg, not 'under 51 kg'), plus a misquote ('Society', not 'Institute').
- USBM 20 Pa rattle preset: wrong meter basis and an overstated label.
- Window reach: uses only the 6.9 kPa end of the 3.4-6.9 kPa band.
- Morgan 2022: the 1e23-5e23 J 'range' is one estimate quoted two ways.
- Instant-growth model:
  - It anchors at the soles but sizes the blast as a ball growing about its centre, so the energy into the air is 2-4× too low and 'the head sweeps little volume' is false.
  - It omits the momentum needed to lift his centre of mass: GPa-level ground load, and a launch of about 25 km for Chicxulub pure size unless he is bolted down.

Gradual-growth and runaway conclusions stand: the shove sets the limit, and the loop ratio reaches 1 only at the horizon. Keep the instant-growth figures as labelled estimates once these fixes are in.
